baseline.statement: Let $U$ be a minimizer at $r\in(0,1)$, and let $m=e(U)$ and $F=F(U)=V(r)$. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)] \item $0<F\le h(r)<1$, $m+F<1$, and $r\le m\le\frac14(1+\sqrt{1+8r^3})$. Moreover, $m=r$ only if $U=r$ a.e. \item $\mu_Ur^3=1-F-m$ and $\bar k_U=1+F-m$. \item $\ell_U=\Lambda_{r^3}(m,F)$. Hence $U\ge\Lambda_{r^3}(m,F)$ a.e.\ and $\Lambda_{r^3}(m,F)\le m$. \item Let $t>0$. If $0\le m_0\le m_1$ and $y_0\le y_1\le1$, then $\Lambda_t(m_0,y_0)\le\Lambda_t(m_1,y_1)$. Moreover $\Lambda_t$ is strictly increasing in $m$ on $m>0$ and in $y$ on $y<1$. \end{enumerate}

The following hold. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)] \item Let $U$ be a graphon with $t(U)=t_*$, $F(U)\le F_*$ and $|\{U\ne r_*\}|>0$. Then $(e(U),F(U))\in\Omega$. \item The conclusion of (a) holds for every minimizer $U$ at $r_*$ that is not a.e. constant. \item $\pi_*\in\Omega$ and $\Omega\subset\Pi$. \end{enumerate}

entries.checked_scope: All three conclusions for actual unrestricted graphons; also compactness of the parameter region.

baseline.statement: Let $U$ be a graphon, let $H=g_*\circ U$, and define $d(x)=\int_0^1H(x,y)\dd y$, $\eta=\iint H$ and $H^\circ(x,y)=H(x,y)-d(x)-d(y)+\eta$. Then the three terms of \[ H(x,y)-\eta=\big(d(x)-\eta\big)+\big(d(y)-\eta\big)+H^\circ(x,y) \] are pairwise orthogonal in $L^2([0,1]^2)$. Moreover, if $(A,B,C)$ has law $\nu_U$, then \[ \E[g_*(A)^2]-2\E[g_*(A)g_*(B)]+\E[g_*(A)]^2=\|H^\circ\|_2^2\ge0 . \]

entries.checked_scope: Actual L2 orthogonal decomposition and residual-square identity for bounded symmetric kernels, specialized to the critical entropy observable and actual triangle law.

baseline.statement: Let $U$ be a graphon and let $X_1,X_2,X_3$ be independent and uniform on $[0,1]$. Let $\nu_U$ be the law on $[0,1]^3$ of \[ (A,B,C)=\big(U(X_1,X_2),U(X_1,X_3),U(X_2,X_3)\big). \] We call $\nu_U$ the \emph{law of the edge values of a random triangle} in $U$.

entries.checked_scope: Actual pushforward of three independent uniform vertices; probability, cube support, moment identities and full coordinate-permutation invariance proved.

baseline.statement: Let $\gamma>0$. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)] \item Every minimizer of $\Phi_\gamma$ on $[0,1]^2$ lies in $(0,1)^2$ and is a stationary point of $\Phi_\gamma$ with positive semidefinite Hessian matrix. \item The stationary points of $\Phi_\gamma$ in $(0,1)^2$ are $(s_\gamma,s_\gamma)$ and the pairs $(a(z),b(z))$ with $z\in(0,1)$ and $\mu(z)=3\gamma$. \item Every stationary point $(a,b)\in(0,1)^2$ of $\Phi_\gamma$ satisfies $F(B_{a,b})+3\gamma t(B_{a,b})=1-e(B_{a,b})$. \item The map $\gamma\mapsto s_\gamma$ is continuously differentiable and strictly decreasing on $(0,\infty)$, and $s_\gamma\to0$ as $\gamma\to\infty$. Moreover, $C_0(\gamma)=\min_{s\in[0,1]}(h(s)+\gamma s^3)$, the minimum is attained only at $s_\gamma$, and $C_0'(\gamma)=s_\gamma^3$. \end{enumerate}

entries.checked_scope: All four conclusions: interiority and stationary equations, actual nonnegative second variation in every direction, complete scalar stationary list, stationary identity, and C1 decreasing constant root with global scalar minimum and derivative.

baseline.statement: The function $\Delta$ is continuously differentiable on $(0,1)$, with \begin{equation} \Delta'(z)=\frac{\mu'(z)}3\big(\rho(z)^3-s_{\mu(z)/3}^3\big). \end{equation} If $\Delta(z)=0$, then $\rho(z)<s_{\mu(z)/3}$. Moreover $\Delta(z)\to-\frac12$ as $z\to0$, and $\Delta(10^{-3})>0$.

entries.checked_scope: C1 gap, exact derivative, strict density order at a zero, limit minus one half, and proved positivity at 1/1000; no numerical output assumed.

baseline.statement: The following hold. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)] \item $Q$ is strictly increasing on $(0,1)$, and $Q(10^{-3})<1<Q(1/50)$. Hence there is a unique $z_m\in(10^{-3},1/50)$ with $Q(z_m)=1$. \item $(\log\mu)'(z)=(Q(z)-1)/(zL)$ for $z\in(0,1)$. Hence $\mu$ is strictly decreasing on $(0,z_m]$ and strictly increasing on $[z_m,1)$. Moreover, $\mu(z)\to\infty$ as $z\to0$. \item For $z\in(0,1)$ and $\gamma=\mu(z)/3$, the Hessian matrix of $\Phi_\gamma$ at $(a(z),b(z))$ has determinant $(1-Q(z))/(4zb(z)^2)$. \end{enumerate}

entries.checked_scope: Strict monotonicity and numerical brackets for Q, unique fold, multiplier derivative/shape and limit, and exact Hessian determinant. The minimizer restriction follows from actual second variation.

baseline.statement: Let $r_n,r\in(0,1)$ with $r_n\to r$. For every $n$ let $U_n$ be a minimizer at $r_n$, and let $U$ be a graphon with $\delta_\cut(U_n,U)\to0$. Then $U$ is a minimizer at $r$, $e(U_n)\to e(U)$, $F(U_n)\to F(U)$ and $\mu_{U_n}\to\mu_U$.

baseline.statement: Let $\theta=(\theta_0,\dots,\theta_{11})\in\R^{12}$ and $\lambda\ge0$. The \emph{certificate function} is \begin{equation} \Psi_{\theta,\lambda}(u;\pi)=-\sum_{i=0}^{11}\theta_i\mathcal E_i(u;\pi)-\lambda\mathcal H_*(u;\pi), \quad u\in(0,\infty)^3,\quad\pi\in\R^2 . \end{equation}

baseline.statement: Let $\theta\in\R^{12}$, $\lambda\ge0$ and $u\in(0,\infty)^3$. The map $\pi\mapsto\Psi_{\theta,\lambda}(u;\pi)$ is concave on $\R^2$. In particular, if $\pi=\sum_{v\in\mathcal V}\alpha_vv$ for a finite set $\mathcal V\subset\R^2$ and weights $\alpha_v\ge0$ of sum one, then $\Psi_{\theta,\lambda}(u;\pi)\ge\sum_{v\in\mathcal V}\alpha_v\Psi_{\theta,\lambda}(u;v)$.
